full_judgment:
Mahfuzur Rahman J: This Rule under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against an order passed by Subordinate Judge, 3rd, Court, Dhaka on 30-11-97 in Partition Suit No.176 of 1995 staying all further proceeding of Execution Case No. 16 of 1995 pending in the Court of the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka till the disposal of the suit. 

 Thereafter the opposite party No. 1 filed an application for restoration of the suit after setting aside the ex parte decree in Miscellaneous Case No. 66 of 1994 which was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 28-10-96 and then the petitioner started Execution Case No. 16 of 1995. 

 "it is established that as a person is a tenant he cannot be permitted during the continuance of the tenancy to resist a suit for eviction by his landlord as a subsequent purchaser from a co-sharer without surrendering his possession to his landlord. As, in the instant case, it is found that the petitioner was a tenant under the respondents to whom he paid rents upto December, 1990, he is debarred from setting up a claim of title in himself to resist the decree for eviction." 

 4. On the application by opposite party No. 1 in Partition Suit No. 176 of 1995 under Order 21rule 29 of the Code the learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 24-7-96 stayed further proceedings of SCC Suit No. 8 of 1994 pending in the Court of the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. The petitioners also on 11-8-96 filed an application for setting aside the stay order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge in Partition Suit No. 176 of 1995 and the opposite party No. 1 filed another application on 27-11-96 under Order 21 rule 29 of the Code before the learned Subordinate Judge in the same suit for stay of the proceedings of SCC Suit No. 9 of 1994 and the Execution Case No. 16 of 1995 pending before the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. Both the applications filed by the petitioners dated 11-8-96 and the application filed by opposite party No. 1 dated 27-11-96 were heard by the learned Subordinate Judge who by his order dated 30-11-96 allowed the petition dated 27-11-96 filed by the opposite party No. 1 praying for stay of further proceeding of Execution Case No. 16 of 1995 and dismissed the petition dated 11-6-96 filed by the petitioners for setting aside the order dated 24-7-96 staying the further proceeding of SCC Suit No. 8 of 1994. 

 6. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that in view of the established legal position as enunciated by the Appellate Division in the case of Md Atiqullah vs Mrs Sanawara Begum and others, reported in 1996 BLD (AD) 260, the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law resulting in his decision occasioning serious failure of justice in passing the impugned order. He further submits that in the aforesaid case the Appellate Division clearly held that a tenant cannot be permitted during the continuance of the tenancy to resist a suit for eviction by his landlord without surrendering his possession to his landlord, the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in his decision resulting in an error of law occasioning serious failure of justice. He lastly, contends that both the suits are not in the same Court and Order 21 rule 29 of the Code has got no manner of application in this case when the proceedings as stayed are not pending in the same Court. 

 Admittedly both the suits are not in the same Court and the impugned order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is absolutely illegal and has got no manner of application in this case. In the decision referred by Mr. Islam reported in 1996 BLD (AD) 260 their Lordships have also referred: 

 "This consistent view of the Appellate Division is that once it is found that a person is a tenant he cannot be permitted during the continuance of the tenancy to resist a suit for eviction by his landlord as a subsequent purchaser from a co-sharer without surrendering his possession to his landlord. In the instant case, the petitioner was found as a tenant under the respondents to whom he had paid rent and as such, he is debarred from setting up a claim-of title in himself to resist the decree for eviction." 

 10. In the result the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka on 30-11-97 staying the Execution Case No. 16 of 1995 of the Court of the Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka is hereby set aside.
